how_to_obtain.instruction: On AWS, simulate s3:PutBucketLogging against the data-access IAM role using the IAM policy simulator to determine whether routine data roles can silence server access logs.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Result should show EvalDecision=implicitDeny or explicitDeny for all principals. Any allowed result sets this attribute to true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On GCP, list custom and predefined roles bound to data-access service accounts and grep for storage.buckets.update, which grants the ability to modify logging configuration.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud projects get-iam-policy <project-id> --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.members[] | test("serviceAccount:<data-sa>")) | .role' | xargs -I{} gcloud iam roles describe {} --format='json' | jq '.includedPermissions[] | select(test("storage.buckets.update"))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No output indicates storage.buckets.update is absent from data-access role effective permissions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Azure, verify that data-access service principals do not have Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/write or the ability to modify diagnostic settings via Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings/write.
how_to_obtain.command: az role definition list --query "[?contains(permissions[0].actions, 'Microsoft.Storage/storageAccounts/blobServices/write')].{Name:name, Actions:permissions[0].actions}" --output json
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Data-access principals should only be assigned roles whose actions list excludes diagnostic settings and blob service configuration writes.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the IAM policy or role definition documents for all service accounts tagged as data-access. Confirm that an explicit Deny statement or absence of logging-configuration actions is documented in the access control matrix.
how_to_obtain.navigation: IAM Policy documentation review; service account inventory register; cloud access control matrix
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Access control matrix explicitly marks logging-configuration permissions as absent or denied for all data-access identities.

typical_values: true (often seen when using aws:s3FullAccess or equivalent broad managed policies without customization)

option_description: Controls whether administrative storage operations — including permission changes, object deletion, logging configuration toggles, and bucket policy modifications — require step-up authentication (MFA), approval workflows (PAM/ITSM gates), or break-glass procedures beyond the baseline credential used for normal access.
security_impact: The Rego policy uses `privileged_action_requires_additional_authz` as a mitigating control: when `data_access_account_can_disable_logging == true`, the `insufficient_privilege_separation_for_storage_roles` finding is suppressed only if this attribute is also true. Without this control, a single compromised credential is sufficient to both exfiltrate data and destroy the audit trail in a single session. It also reduces the blast radius of credential theft by requiring attackers to satisfy an additional authentication factor before executing destructive or privilege-escalating operations.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On AWS, inspect bucket policies and SCPs for IAM condition keys such as aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent, aws:MultiFactorAuthAge, or s3:ResourceAccount that gate privilege-sensitive actions. Check for explicit Deny on admin actions when MFA is absent.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <bucket-name> | jq '.Policy | fromjson | .Statement[] | select(.Condition.BoolIfExists["aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent"] or .Condition.Bool["aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent"])'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy statements should include an explicit Deny block with Condition: Bool: aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent: false for privileged actions such as s3:PutBucketPolicy and s3:DeleteObject.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Service Control Policies at the AWS Organization level for MFA enforcement on storage admin actions.
how_to_obtain.command: aws organizations list-policies --filter SERVICE_CONTROL_POLICY --query 'Policies[*].Id' --output text | xargs -I{} aws organizations describe-policy --policy-id {} --query 'Policy.Content' --output text | jq 'select(.Statement[].Condition.BoolIfExists["aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent"] != null)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: SCPs should contain deny rules conditioned on absence of MFA for sensitive S3 actions applicable to the storage account's organization unit.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the cloud operations or IAM team to confirm whether a PAM (Privileged Access Management) tool such as CyberArk, HashiCorp Boundary, or AWS IAM Identity Center with approval workflows gates elevation to storage admin roles. Request evidence of an approval workflow audit log for a recent privileged storage action.
how_to_obtain.navigation: PAM tool admin console → Session recordings or approval requests → filter for storage-admin role assumptions
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Evidence of time-bound, approval-gated role assumption or session recording for any administrative storage operation in the past 30 days.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In AWS IAM Identity Center (SSO), navigate to Permission Sets used for storage administration and confirm that MFA is set to required, or that session duration is set to a short window with re-authentication enforced.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console → IAM Identity Center → Permission Sets → [storage-admin set] → Multi-factor authentication → Require MFA
how_to_obtain.expected_output: MFA setting shows 'Require them to provide a one-time password each time they sign in' or equivalent; Session duration is ≤1 hour.

typical_values: false (default; most environments do not enforce MFA conditions on bucket policies)
true (mature environments with SCPs or PAM tooling)

option_description: Controls whether the storage bucket retains prior versions of every object upon modification or deletion. When enabled, a delete operation places a delete marker rather than permanently removing the object, and overwrites create a new version while preserving the previous one.
security_impact: The Rego policy references `object_versioning_enabled` in two rules. In `missing_object_versioning_and_delete_protection`, the exposure fires when both versioning and object lock are absent, and also when versioning is enabled but neither object lock nor MFA delete provide additional protection. In `absence_of_integrity_verification_for_stored_objects`, absence of versioning combined with absent checksum validation triggers the integrity finding. Without versioning, ransomware or malicious insiders can permanently destroy data by overwriting objects, with no recovery path outside of external backups.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On AWS, retrieve the versioning configuration for a specific S3 bucket. A Status of Enabled confirms versioning is active; Suspended or absent output indicates it is disabled.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: {"Status": "Enabled", "MFADelete": "Disabled"} — Status must be Enabled; absence of the Status key or Suspended means versioning is off.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On GCP, retrieve the bucket metadata and inspect the versioning configuration block.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: gs://<bucket-name>: Enabled — any other output (e.g., Suspended) indicates versioning is not active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Azure, Azure Blob Storage versioning is a storage account-level property. Retrieve the blob service properties to check versioning enablement.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: true — false or null indicates versioning is disabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In AWS Console, navigate to S3 → [bucket] → Properties → Bucket Versioning section. In GCP Console, navigate to Cloud Storage → [bucket] → Configuration → Object versioning.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console → S3 → [bucket] → Properties → Bucket Versioning | GCP Console → Cloud Storage → [bucket] → Configuration → Object versioning
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Status shows 'Enabled' (AWS) or a green checkmark with 'On' (GCP).

typical_values: false (default for new buckets on all major providers)
true (required for compliance-sensitive workloads; commonly enabled in regulated industries)

option_description: Controls whether WORM (Write Once Read Many) object lock or an equivalent immutable-storage mechanism is enabled on the bucket, preventing objects from being deleted or overwritten during a defined retention period regardless of IAM permissions, including by the bucket owner.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires `missing_object_versioning_and_delete_protection` when both `object_versioning_enabled` and `object_lock_enabled` are false, and also when versioning is true but object lock and MFA delete are both absent. Object lock is the only control that enforces immutability even against privileged identities, making it the primary defense against ransomware that compromises admin credentials. Without it, an attacker with sufficient IAM rights can permanently destroy all object versions, defeating versioning protections.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On AWS, retrieve the object lock configuration for the bucket. Object lock must be enabled at bucket creation time on S3; it cannot be added retroactively.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: {"ObjectLockConfiguration": {"ObjectLockEnabled": "Enabled", "Rule": {"DefaultRetention": {"Mode": "COMPLIANCE", "Days": 30}}}} — ObjectLockEnabled must be Enabled with a DefaultRetention rule present.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On GCP, check the bucket's retention policy, which is the GCS equivalent of object lock. A locked retention policy enforces WORM behavior.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Retention Policy (LOCKED): Duration 2592000s — the LOCKED status confirms immutability; an unlocked policy or absence of output indicates object lock is not in effect.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Azure, check whether immutability policies are configured on the blob container using the Azure CLI.
how_to_obtain.command: az storage container immutability-policy show --account-name <storage-account> --container-name <container> --resource-group <rg> --output json
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A policy with state=Locked and immutabilityPeriodSinceCreationInDays > 0 confirms object lock is active. A 404 or empty response indicates it is absent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In AWS Console, navigate to S3 → [bucket] → Properties → Object Lock section. Note that a bucket created without Object Lock enabled cannot have it enabled after creation.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console → S3 → [bucket] → Properties → Object Lock → scroll to Object lock configuration
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Object lock status shows 'Enabled' with a retention mode (Compliance or Governance) and a configured retention period.

typical_values: false (default; most buckets are created without Object Lock)
true (required for SEC 17a-4, FINRA, HIPAA, and other immutable-record compliance frameworks)

option_description: Controls whether multi-factor authentication is required to permanently delete object versions (i.e., delete a specific version rather than add a delete marker) or to change the versioning state of the bucket. This is an S3-specific control requiring the MFA device serial and token to be passed in the request header.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires `missing_object_versioning_and_delete_protection` when `object_versioning_enabled` is true but both `object_lock_enabled` and `mfa_delete_enabled` are false. Versioning alone only soft-deletes objects; an attacker who obtains the IAM credentials can call DeleteObjectVersion in a loop to permanently purge all versions. MFA delete forces possession of a physical or virtual MFA device in addition to the IAM credential, creating a two-factor barrier against version purging that cannot be bypassed by credential compromise alone.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On AWS, retrieve the versioning configuration for the bucket and inspect the MFADelete field. This field only appears with a non-empty value when MFA delete has been explicitly configured.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: {"Status": "Enabled", "MFADelete": "Enabled"} — MFADelete must be Enabled. A value of Disabled or absence of the key means MFA delete is not active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt to enable MFA delete (in a test environment) to confirm current state. The command will fail with an authentication error if MFA delete is already configured and your current session lacks MFA, confirming it is enforced.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Successful execution with no error confirms MFA delete can be enabled; note that enabling MFA delete requires the AWS account root user credentials.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use the S3 GetBucketVersioning REST API directly, authenticating with a root-account session, to retrieve the MFADelete element from the XML response body.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Enabled — any other value or empty output means MFA delete is not active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the storage administrator or cloud operations team. MFA delete on S3 requires the account root user to enable it and requires physical MFA device availability. Confirm whether the root account has an MFA device registered and whether a documented procedure exists for version deletion requests.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console → IAM → Account settings → Root user MFA | Internal runbook for permanent version deletion procedures
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documentation confirms MFA delete is enabled on critical buckets and a process exists requiring MFA device possession for any permanent deletion operation.

typical_values: false (default and extremely common; MFA delete is rarely configured due to root-account requirement complexity)
true (uncommon; primarily seen in high-security financial or government workloads)

option_description: Controls whether the storage platform enforces hard namespace boundaries — through bucket/container policies, storage account ACLs, or resource-level IAM — that prevent one tenant's processes or accounts from accessing another tenant's storage namespace at the platform level.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires `cross_tenant_isolation_misconfiguration` both when `namespace_isolation_enforced` is false (directly) and when `shared_credential_scope == per_service` combined with the absence of namespace isolation. Without enforced namespace boundaries, a compromised or misbehaving tenant process that obtains a service-level credential can enumerate and access all other tenants' buckets or containers within the same service account. This is a critical multi-tenancy breach scenario that bypasses application-layer authorization entirely.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On AWS, retrieve bucket policies for each tenant's bucket and confirm that a Deny condition explicitly rejects cross-account or cross-principal access. Verify that no bucket is accessible via wildcard principal.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <tenant-bucket-name> | jq '.Policy | fromjson | .Statement[] | select(.Effect=="Allow") | {Principal:.Principal, Actions:.Action, Resource:.Resource}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Principal should reference only the specific tenant's account ID or role ARN, not '*' or other tenant account IDs. Any cross-account Allow without explicit tenant scoping fails isolation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On GCP, list all IAM bindings on a tenant bucket and verify that no bindings reference service accounts from other tenant projects.
how_to_obtain.command: gsutil iam get gs://<tenant-bucket> | jq '.bindings[] | {role:.role, members:.members}' | grep -v '<tenant-project-number>'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No results after grep — any service account not belonging to the tenant's project appearing in bindings indicates a namespace isolation failure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On Azure, use the ARM REST API to list container-level access policies for a storage account hosting multiple tenant containers, confirming each container uses stored access policies scoped to the respective tenant's service principal.
how_to_obtain.command: az storage container list --account-name <shared-storage-account> --output json | jq '.[].properties.publicAccess' && az storage container policy list --account-name <shared-storage-account> --container-name <tenant-container> --output json
how_to_obtain.expected_output: publicAccess should be null or off for each container. Stored access policies should reference only the specific tenant's managed identity or service principal.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the multi-tenant architecture documentation and IAM design patterns to confirm whether tenant namespaces are enforced at the platform layer (separate accounts per tenant, VPC endpoint policies, or bucket policies with account conditions) versus solely at the application layer.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Architecture review documentation; tenant onboarding runbook; IAM role assignment matrix
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Architecture documents confirm platform-layer enforcement: either separate AWS accounts per tenant, per-tenant GCP projects, or explicit deny-by-default bucket policies with explicit per-tenant allow conditions.

typical_values: true (recommended; enforced in well-designed multi-tenant SaaS platforms using separate accounts or explicit deny policies)
false (common in early-stage SaaS relying solely on application-layer authorization)

option_description: Describes the blast radius of credentials used by the storage service — whether a single credential or role can access all tenants' namespaces globally, is scoped to a single service (accessing multiple tenants), or is uniquely provisioned per tenant with access to only that tenant's namespace.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires `cross_tenant_isolation_misconfiguration` when `shared_credential_scope == global` unconditionally, and also when `shared_credential_scope == per_service` combined with `namespace_isolation_enforced` being false. A global credential is a single point of compromise that exposes all tenant data simultaneously. A per-service credential with absent namespace isolation still permits lateral movement across all tenants served by that service. Only per_tenant credentials with namespace isolation enforced fully contain the blast radius of a credential compromise to a single tenant's data.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On AWS, list the IAM roles or access keys used by storage-access services and inspect their attached policies to determine whether the Resource ARN is scoped to a single tenant's bucket prefix or uses a wildcard covering all buckets.
how_to_obtain.command: aws iam list-attached-role-policies --role-name <storage-service-role> --output json | jq '.AttachedPolicies[].PolicyArn' | xargs -I{} aws iam get-policy-version --policy-arn {} --version-id $(aws iam get-policy --policy-arn {} --query 'Policy.DefaultVersionId' --output text) --query 'PolicyVersion.Document.Statement[*].Resource'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Resources should be specific bucket ARNs or prefixed ARNs such as arn:aws:s3:::tenant-<id>-bucket/*. A wildcard arn:aws:s3:::* indicates global scope.

how_to_obtain.instruction: On GCP, inspect service account key usage and the IAM bindings it holds across all storage buckets to determine the number of distinct tenant buckets accessible from a single service account.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud asset search-all-iam-policies --scope=projects/<project-id> --query='policy:serviceAccount:<storage-sa>@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com' --format='json' | jq '[.[] | select(.resource | test("storage.googleapis.com"))] | length'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Count of 1 indicates per-tenant scoping. A count equal to the total number of tenant buckets indicates per_service or global scope.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the platform engineering or DevOps team responsible for storage credential provisioning. Request the credential issuance runbook and confirm whether a separate service account or IAM role is created for each tenant at onboarding, or whether a shared service identity is used across all tenants.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Tenant onboarding runbook; service account creation automation scripts; Terraform/Pulumi IAM module definitions
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Runbook confirms per-tenant service account creation with resource-scoped IAM bindings; or flags shared service account as a known risk with namespace isolation as a compensating control.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review Terraform, CloudFormation, or Pulumi infrastructure-as-code templates defining IAM roles and service accounts for storage access. Search for role resource policies and identify whether bucket ARNs use per-tenant prefixes, per-service wildcards, or global wildcards.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No matches with wildcard bucket references in data-access role definitions. Each role's Resource block should reference a tenant-specific bucket name pattern.

typical_values: per_service (most common in SaaS platforms using a single application service identity)
global (common in early-stage or internally built platforms; highest risk)
per_tenant (best practice; common in compliance-regulated multi-tenant platforms)

option_description: Controls whether automated policy scanning has identified IAM policies, ACL entries, or role bindings that incorrectly grant one tenant's principal access to another tenant's storage namespace. This is a detection output attribute representing the result of running cross-tenant policy audit tooling against all storage namespaces in a multi-tenant environment.
security_impact: Directly triggers the cross_tenant_isolation_misconfiguration Rego rule when set to true. The policy flags this condition because cross-tenant access violations mean sensitive data belonging to one customer or organizational unit is readable or writable by another tenant's credentials — a critical data isolation failure. Even a single policy misconfiguration can expose the entire namespace of an affected tenant, bypassing all application-layer access controls.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run AWS IAM Access Analyzer scoped to S3 bucket policies to detect cross-account or cross-tenant access grants across all buckets in the account.
how_to_obtain.command: aws accessanalyzer list-findings --analyzer-arn $(aws accessanalyzer list-analyzers --query 'analyzers[0].arn' --output text) --filter '{"resourceType":{"eq":["AWS::S3::Bucket"]}}' --query 'findings[?status==`ACTIVE`].[resource,principal,condition]' --output table
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Table of active findings showing bucket ARNs with external or cross-account principal grants. Empty output indicates no cross-tenant violations detected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use a CSPM tool API (e.g., Prisma Cloud, Wiz, Orca) to query for cross-tenant policy findings across all storage resources and export results.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON array of findings. An empty array or findings with status 'closed' indicates no active cross-tenant violations.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCS, use the gcloud asset inventory to enumerate all bucket IAM policies and flag bindings that reference principals outside the expected project or organization domain.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud asset search-all-iam-policies --scope='organizations/<ORG_ID>' --query='resource:storage.googleapis.com/buckets' --format=json | jq '[.[] | select(.policy.bindings[].members[] | test("@external-tenant")) | {resource: .resource, members: .policy.bindings[].members}]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON list of bucket resources with external-tenant principal bindings. No output confirms isolation is intact.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Azure Portal, navigate to Storage Accounts > Select each account > Access Control (IAM) > Role Assignments. Filter by 'External' principals and review any role assignments referencing service principals or users outside your tenant's directory.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Azure Portal > Storage Accounts > [Account Name] > Access Control (IAM) > Role Assignments > Filter: Type = External
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No external principals listed under role assignments. Any entries with external GUIDs or cross-directory identities represent policy violations.

typical_values: null (audit tooling not yet run; treat as unknown/high-risk)

option_description: Indicates whether an explicit data retention or lifecycle policy is actively configured on the storage host to automatically expire, archive, or delete data objects after a defined period. This covers S3 lifecycle rules, Azure Blob retention policies, GCS object lifecycle management rules, and database TTL settings.
security_impact: A missing retention policy is the primary trigger for the missing_data_classification_and_retention_policy_enforcement Rego rule. When false, the rule flags the exposure unconditionally. Absent retention policies mean data accumulates indefinitely, expanding the attack surface: every additional retained object containing sensitive data is an additional exposure if the storage is compromised, and indefinite retention may violate regulatory requirements (GDPR right to erasure, HIPAA minimum necessary, PCI DSS data retention limits).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check S3 bucket lifecycle configuration to verify at least one rule is active with an expiration or transition action defined.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration --bucket <BUCKET_NAME> --query 'Rules[?Status==`Enabled`].[ID,Filter,Expiration,Transitions]' --output table 2>&1 | grep -v 'NoSuchLifecycleConfiguration' || echo 'NO_LIFECYCLE_POLICY'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Table of enabled rules with expiration or transition actions. Output of 'NO_LIFECYCLE_POLICY' confirms retention_policy_configured = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCS, list object lifecycle rules on the bucket to verify retention actions exist.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud storage buckets describe gs://<BUCKET_NAME> --format='json(lifecycle)' | jq '.lifecycle.rule[] | select(.action.type == "Delete" or .action.type == "SetStorageClass") | {condition: .condition, action: .action}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON objects describing lifecycle rules with Delete or SetStorageClass actions. Empty output means no retention policy is configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Azure Portal, navigate to Storage Account > Data Management > Lifecycle Management to review active lifecycle policies, or check Immutability Policies under Blob Containers.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Azure Portal > Storage Accounts > [Account Name] > Data Management > Lifecycle Management > View/Edit Rules
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At least one active rule with a 'Delete blob' or 'Move to archive' action and a defined day threshold. No rules listed means retention_policy_configured = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Azure REST API to retrieve lifecycle management policies for a storage account.
how_to_obtain.command: az storage account management-policy show --account-name <STORAGE_ACCOUNT> --resource-group <RG> --query 'policy.rules[?enabled==`true`].[name,definition.actions]' --output table 2>&1 || echo 'NO_POLICY'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Table of enabled policy rules with defined actions. 'NO_POLICY' or empty output confirms no lifecycle policy.

typical_values: true (lifecycle rule configured with expiration actions)
false (no retention policy — common in development and legacy environments)

option_description: Indicates whether data stored on the host has classification labels (e.g., PII, sensitive, confidential, restricted) applied at the storage resource level — either via cloud provider tagging, metadata attributes, or data catalog integration — and whether these labels are actively driving lifecycle and retention enforcement decisions.
security_impact: Works in combination with retention_policy_configured and oldest_unreviewed_data_age_days in the missing_data_classification_and_retention_policy_enforcement Rego rule. Specifically, if retention_policy_configured is true but data_classification_labels_applied is false and oldest_unreviewed_data_age_days exceeds 90, the exposure fires. Additionally, if classification labels are absent and data is over 365 days old, the rule triggers regardless of retention policy state. Without labels, retention policies cannot be applied with appropriate granularity to different sensitivity tiers, leading to either over-retention of sensitive data or premature deletion of required records.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List all tags applied to an S3 bucket and verify the presence of classification-related tag keys (e.g., DataClassification, Sensitivity, DataType).
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-tagging --bucket <BUCKET_NAME> --query 'TagSet[?Key==`DataClassification` || Key==`Sensitivity` || Key==`data-classification`]' --output table 2>&1 || echo 'NO_TAGS'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Tag entries with classification keys and values (e.g., DataClassification=PII). 'NO_TAGS' or empty output means data_classification_labels_applied = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCS, describe the bucket to retrieve labels and check for classification-related label keys.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud storage buckets describe gs://<BUCKET_NAME> --format='json(labels)' | jq '.labels | to_entries[] | select(.key | test("classification|sensitivity|data.type"; "i"))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Key-value pairs with classification labels. Empty output indicates no classification labels applied.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Azure Blob Storage container or storage account resource tags in Azure Portal, or review Microsoft Purview data catalog scan results for sensitivity label assignments.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Azure Portal > Storage Accounts > [Account Name] > Tags OR Microsoft Purview > Data Catalog > Search [storage resource] > Sensitivity Labels
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Tags or sensitivity labels with values like 'Confidential', 'PII', 'Restricted'. No labels means data_classification_labels_applied = false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use AWS Macie to determine if the bucket has been scanned and if sensitive data findings exist, indicating whether classification is actively assessed.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Completed classification job entries for the bucket. No results mean no active classification scan has been run, implying labels may be absent.

typical_values: false (most common — tagging is often manual and inconsistent)
true (enforced via automated tagging pipelines or IaC templates)

option_description: The age in days of the oldest data object or record on the storage host that has not been subject to a retention review, expiry, or deletion action. This is calculated from the creation or last-modified timestamp of the oldest object lacking a deletion or archival marker to the current date.
security_impact: Used as a threshold-based trigger in two conditions of the missing_data_classification_and_retention_policy_enforcement Rego rule: (1) if retention policy exists but classification labels are absent, the rule fires when this value exceeds 90 days; (2) if classification labels are absent regardless of retention policy, the rule fires when this value exceeds 365 days. A large value indicates data has accumulated without any governance review, meaning sensitive historical records may be retained well beyond their required period, multiplying data exposure risk and regulatory liability over time.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Find the oldest object in an S3 bucket by listing all objects sorted by LastModified and returning the oldest, then calculate its age in days.
how_to_obtain.command: OLDEST=$(aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket <BUCKET_NAME> --query 'sort_by(Contents, &LastModified)[0].[Key,LastModified]' --output text); OLDEST_DATE=$(echo $OLDEST | awk '{print $2}'); echo "Oldest object: $OLDEST"; echo "Age in days: $(( ($(date +%s) - $(date -d "$OLDEST_DATE" +%s)) / 86400 ))"
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Object key, last-modified timestamp, and calculated age in days. Values over 90 or 365 may trigger the retention policy exposure rule.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCS, use gsutil to list objects sorted by time created and calculate the age of the oldest unarchived object.
how_to_obtain.command: gsutil ls -l gs://<BUCKET_NAME>/** | sort -k2 | head -5 | awk '{print $2, $3}' && echo 'Calculate days from oldest date to today manually or pipe to date arithmetic.'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Oldest object creation dates and their paths. Oldest timestamp converted to days gives the oldest_unreviewed_data_age_days value.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query Azure Blob Storage to find the oldest blob by CreatedOn timestamp using Azure CLI.
how_to_obtain.command: az storage blob list --container-name <CONTAINER> --account-name <STORAGE_ACCOUNT> --query 'sort_by([],&properties.creationTime)[0].[name,properties.creationTime]' --output table --auth-mode login
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Oldest blob name and creation timestamp. Calculate days elapsed to determine the attribute value.

how_to_obtain.instruction: If object creation timestamps are not directly queryable, analyze storage access or audit logs for the earliest recorded write event to estimate the oldest object age.
how_to_obtain.command: aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name '/aws/s3/<BUCKET_NAME>' --filter-pattern '{$.eventName=PutObject}' --query 'sort_by(events,&timestamp)[0].[timestamp,message]' --output table 2>/dev/null || echo 'Check CloudTrail S3 data events for earliest PutObject timestamp.'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Earliest PutObject event timestamp from which object age can be derived.

typical_values: 1000+ (legacy environments or cold storage with no retention enforcement)

option_description: Indicates whether the storage service or client enforces checksum or hash validation (e.g., MD5, SHA-256, CRC32) when reading or writing stored objects. When enabled, the storage layer computes and verifies a hash of object data on put/get operations to detect corruption or unauthorized content modification in transit to/from storage.
security_impact: Triggers the absence_of_integrity_verification_for_stored_objects Rego rule under two conditions: (1) when false and object versioning is also disabled, the rule fires immediately; (2) when false and integrity_monitoring_policy is 'none', the rule also fires. Without checksum validation, silent data corruption from hardware faults, bit rot, or deliberate tampering of stored objects cannot be detected at the storage layer. An attacker with write access could modify objects without triggering any integrity alert, or corrupted data could be served to applications without detection.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS S3, verify if a bucket policy or server-side validation enforces checksum algorithms by checking if object metadata contains checksum fields (x-amz-checksum-*) and whether bucket policy denies uploads without checksums.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <BUCKET_NAME> --query 'Policy' --output text | python3 -m json.tool | grep -i 'checksum\|x-amz-checksum' || echo 'No checksum enforcement policy found'; aws s3api head-object --bucket <BUCKET_NAME> --key <SAMPLE_OBJECT_KEY> --checksum-mode ENABLED --query '[ChecksumCRC32,ChecksumSHA256,ChecksumSHA1]' --output table
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Bucket policy containing checksum condition keys, and head-object response showing populated checksum fields. Missing checksum values indicate validation is not enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCS, check if object metadata includes MD5 or CRC32c hash fields by inspecting object metadata, which GCS automatically computes but clients must validate.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud storage objects describe gs://<BUCKET_NAME>/<OBJECT_NAME> --format='json(md5Hash,crc32c,customerEncryption)' | jq '{md5Hash: .md5Hash, crc32c: .crc32c}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON with md5Hash and crc32c values populated. Presence indicates GCS stores hashes; client-side validation must also be confirmed in application code or SDK config.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review application or SDK configuration files for checksum validation settings (e.g., boto3 config, Azure SDK options, GCS client config) to confirm client-enforced checksum validation is enabled.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration entries with checksum validation enabled (e.g., 'checksum_mode = enabled', 'ChecksumAlgorithm: SHA256'). No results suggest client-side validation is not configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Azure Blob, verify Content-MD5 header enforcement by checking if blob upload requests include content-md5 and whether the service validates it, using the Azure REST API to inspect blob properties.
how_to_obtain.command: az storage blob show --container-name <CONTAINER> --name <BLOB_NAME> --account-name <STORAGE_ACCOUNT> --auth-mode login --query 'properties.contentMd5' --output tsv
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A base64-encoded MD5 hash string. Null or empty value indicates checksum was not provided or validated at write time.

typical_values: false (default for most cloud storage configurations — checksum must be explicitly enabled)
true (enforced via SDK configuration or bucket policy conditions requiring checksum headers)

option_description: The level of integrity monitoring configured for stored objects, representing a spectrum from no monitoring ('none') to metadata-only checks ('metadata_only' — e.g., size and last-modified timestamp), to hash computed at write time but not validated on read ('hash_on_write'), to full cryptographic hash validation on both write and read operations ('hash_on_read_write').
security_impact: The absence_of_integrity_verification_for_stored_objects Rego rule fires when integrity_monitoring_policy is 'none' and object_checksum_validation_enabled is also false. A policy of 'none' provides no tamper detection capability whatsoever — an attacker who gains write access to stored objects can modify content without any integrity alert being generated. Even 'metadata_only' and 'hash_on_write' provide incomplete protection: metadata checks cannot detect content modification, and write-only hashes cannot detect tampering that occurs after the initial write. Only 'hash_on_read_write' provides comprehensive integrity assurance.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview storage administrators or review IaC templates (Terraform, CloudFormation, Bicep) to determine the designed integrity monitoring approach for the storage resource.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IaC resource definitions showing checksum algorithm settings, versioning configuration, or object lock settings that indicate the intended integrity monitoring level.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS S3, determine integrity policy level by checking versioning (necessary for hash_on_read_write), existing object checksum metadata, and bucket policy checksum enforcement conditions.
how_to_obtain.command: echo '=== Versioning ==='; aws s3api get-bucket-versioning --bucket <BUCKET_NAME>; echo '=== Sample Object Checksum ==='; aws s3api head-object --bucket <BUCKET_NAME> --key <SAMPLE_KEY> --checksum-mode ENABLED 2>/dev/null | grep -i checksum; echo '=== Bucket Policy Checksum Conditions ==='; aws s3api get-bucket-policy --bucket <BUCKET_NAME> 2>/dev/null | python3 -m json.tool | grep -i checksum
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Versioning status (Enabled/Suspended/none), checksum fields populated on object head (indicates hash_on_write or hash_on_read_write), and bucket policy checksum conditions. Absence of all indicates 'none'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review application-layer storage middleware or SDK wrapper configurations to identify if read-time hash validation (hash_on_read_write) is implemented programmatically beyond native storage service capabilities.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Code or config entries showing read-time hash validation logic. Absence means the policy is at most 'hash_on_write' even if checksums are stored at write time.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In AWS Console, check S3 bucket Properties for Default Encryption and Versioning status, then inspect individual object properties for checksum algorithm fields to assess the effective integrity monitoring level.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console > S3 > [Bucket] > Properties > Versioning (check status) AND S3 > [Bucket] > [Object] > Properties > Checksum (check algorithm field)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Versioning status and checksum algorithm (e.g., SHA-256, CRC32) shown in object properties. No checksum algorithm and disabled versioning maps to 'none'; versioning + checksum maps to 'hash_on_write' at minimum.

typical_values: none (most common default — no integrity controls configured)
metadata_only (object size and ETag checks only, common in basic deployments)
hash_on_write (checksum stored at upload, not re-validated on read)
hash_on_read_write (least common — requires explicit SDK/policy configuration)
